note: Each corrects a statement in a new verdict's text that the case's prompt or policyengine-us 2.41.0 contradicts. Two independent reviewers (Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, neither part of the release) read all 26 new texts against each case's prompt and the engine, and a review of the release's pull request found three more of scenario_015's Medicaid texts that the household's calculation contradicts and a misstated EITC end point in scenario_014 (docs/release_20261013b/design.md). Each correction here was then checked against the engine's code and parameters, and for scenario_015's Medicaid pathway against a calculation of that household. None changes a class, a flag, an exclusion or a score.

amendments.old: PolicyEngine's aged/blind/disabled pathway applies SSI-style income limits plus a small resource cap.
amendments.new: PolicyEngine's aged/blind/disabled pathway in Indiana requires the head to be aged, blind or disabled under SSI's rules, countable income within 100% of the poverty guideline and resources under $2,000.
amendments.reason: The text stated Indiana's rule as a general fact and called the income limit SSI-style. Indiana's parameters under gov.hhs.medicaid.eligibility.categories.senior_or_disabled: income limit 1.00 of the poverty guideline (income/limit/individual.yaml), not the SSI federal benefit rate (uses_ssi_federal_benefit_rate.yaml: false), and a $2,000 individual asset limit (assets/limit/individual.yaml), tested as assets below the limit. The pathway's first condition is is_ssi_aged_blind_disabled (is_optional_senior_or_disabled_for_medicaid), which holds for a person who is SSI-aged, blind or SSI-disabled.

amendments.old: Roughly $45,000 of earnings and about $585,000 in bank and stock assets fail both tests, so medicaid_category is NONE.
amendments.new: Earnings of $45,000 are above SSI's substantial gainful activity limit, so PolicyEngine does not count the head as disabled for this pathway, and about $585,000 in bank and stock assets is far above the resource cap, so medicaid_category is NONE.
amendments.reason: The engine's income test does not fail here; the disability condition and the asset test do. Computed for this household on policyengine-us 2.41.0: meets_ssi_disability_criteria False, ssi_engaged_in_sga True, is_ssi_disabled False, is_optional_senior_or_disabled_income_eligible True (medicaid_optional_senior_or_disabled_countable_income 0), is_optional_senior_or_disabled_asset_eligible False (ssi_countable_resources 584,850), medicaid_category NONE. ssi_engaged_in_sga compares monthly ssi_earned_income ($3,750) with gov.ssa.sga.non_blind ($1,690 in 2026), and is_ssi_disabled is meets_ssi_disability_criteria and not ssi_engaged_in_sga. The conclusion does not rest on the unlisted meets_ssi_disability_criteria input, which the household data never set: computed with it set to True, ssi_engaged_in_sga keeps is_ssi_disabled False and medicaid_category stays NONE.

amendments.old: Both models treated the disability flag by itself as qualifying
amendments.new: One model treated the disability flag by itself as qualifying and the other wrongly asserted that the head met the disability pathway's limits
amendments.reason: Only minimax-m3 relied on the flag alone. claude-sonnet-5's reasoning in the case's prompt says the head's income is 'well below the SSI/disability-related Medicaid threshold' and that earnings 'plus assets fall within eligibility limits'. The engine's income test passes for this household, so the text names the pathway's limits rather than its income limit: what fails is the disability condition, because earnings exceed SSI's substantial gainful activity limit, and the asset test. Computed for this household on policyengine-us 2.41.0: ssi_earned_income $45,000, so $3,750 a month against gov.ssa.sga.non_blind of $1,690 a month in 2026; ssi_engaged_in_sga True; is_ssi_disabled False; medicaid_optional_senior_or_disabled_countable_income 0 against a limit of $15,960, so the income test passes; ssi_countable_resources 584,850, so the asset test fails; medicaid_category NONE.

amendments.old: PolicyEngine does not model a working-disabled buy-in with relaxed limits
amendments.new: PolicyEngine models a working-disabled buy-in only for California, Illinois and Mississippi, not Indiana
amendments.reason: True for this household's state but false as a general fact: policyengine-us 2.41.0's is_working_disabled_buy_in_for_medicaid is ca_wdp_eligible or il_hbwd_eligible or ms_wd_eligible, each defined for its own state, and nothing models one for Indiana.

amendments.old: The disability pathway needs SSI-level income and resources, but the head has $45,000 in wages and about $585,000 in assets
amendments.new: In Indiana the disability pathway needs the head to be disabled under SSI's rules, countable income within 100% of the poverty guideline and resources under $2,000, but the head's earnings of $45,000 exceed SSI's substantial gainful activity limit and about $585,000 in assets exceeds the cap
amendments.reason: Indiana's income limit for the pathway is the poverty guideline, not the SSI benefit rate, and the engine's income test passes for this household: what fails is the disability condition and the asset test. Indiana's parameters under gov.hhs.medicaid.eligibility.categories.senior_or_disabled: income limit 1.00 of the poverty guideline (income/limit/individual.yaml), not the SSI federal benefit rate (uses_ssi_federal_benefit_rate.yaml: false), and a $2,000 individual asset limit (assets/limit/individual.yaml), tested as assets below the limit. Computed for this household on policyengine-us 2.41.0: ssi_earned_income $45,000, so $3,750 a month against gov.ssa.sga.non_blind of $1,690 a month in 2026; ssi_engaged_in_sga True; is_ssi_disabled False; medicaid_optional_senior_or_disabled_countable_income 0 against a limit of $15,960, so the income test passes; ssi_countable_resources 584,850, so the asset test fails; medicaid_category NONE.

amendments.old: It also never compared the full $3,022.97 monthly gross income with the 130% gross limit, which the household fails at about 232% of the guideline.
amendments.new: The full $3,022.97 of monthly gross income fails the 130% gross limit, at about 232% of the guideline.
amendments.reason: The model's reasoning in the case's prompt gives an income limit of about $1,655 a month and says 'This household exceeds the income limit', as the annotation's next sentence also reports, so 'never compared' contradicts both.

amendments.old: The model ran the one-child EITC phase-out on a made-up $27,700 AGI.
amendments.new: The model computed the one-child EITC as $4,450 minus 7.65% of ($72,600 − $27,700), but 7.65% is the childless phase-out rate and the one-child rate is 15.98%.
amendments.reason: The model's reasoning in the case's prompt is '2026 max $4,450 minus 7.65% phaseout × ($72,600 - $27,700 AGI) = $1,015': $72,600 is the income and $27,700 the phase-out start, so the phase-out was not run on a $27,700 AGI. policyengine-us 2.41.0's 2026 EITC phase-out rates are 0.0765 with no children and 0.1598 with one (gov.irs.credits.eitc.phase_out.rate).

amendments.old: Most models treated the $1,700 refundability cap as the amount payable and skipped the step
amendments.new: The most common error treated the $1,700 refundability cap as the amount payable and skipped the step
amendments.reason: Six of the eleven models submitted $1,700 and four of them skipped the limit (claude-opus-4.7, claude-opus-4.8, gpt-5.6-luna, ox-alpha); claude-sonnet-5 applied it and then overrode it, and qwen3.8-max applied it to the child's liability. That is the most common error, not most models.

amendments.old: the Recovery Rebate and payroll tax credits are inactive in 2026
amendments.new: the Recovery Rebate and payroll tax credits are $0 in 2026
amendments.reason: The case's prompt says each component returned $0. In policyengine-us 2.41.0 the refundable payroll tax credit is an input with no dated rule (refundable_payroll_tax_credit has no formula), so 'inactive in 2026' fits only the Recovery Rebate.

amendments.old: Any positive figure means the model either invented a child-based credit or applied the with-children EITC schedule.
amendments.new: Any positive figure is incorrect for this household.
amendments.reason: The case's prompt shows every refundable credit component at $0, which supports rejecting any positive answer but not a claim that these two errors are the only way to reach one. policyengine-us 2.41.0's 2026 EITC at $45,000 of earnings for a single filer is $0 with no child (maximum $664), $1,054 with one and $2,870 with two (gov.irs.credits.eitc max, phase_out.start, phase_out.rate), so $1,735.80 fits none of the 2026 schedules.

amendments.old: The EITC figure only fits the with-children phase-out schedule.
amendments.new: The EITC figure does not fit the childless schedule.
amendments.reason: The model's reasoning in the case's prompt gives $1,735.80 without a schedule. policyengine-us 2.41.0's 2026 EITC at $45,000 of earnings for a single filer is $0 with no child (maximum $664), $1,054 with one and $2,870 with two (gov.irs.credits.eitc max, phase_out.start, phase_out.rate), so $1,735.80 fits none of the 2026 schedules. It exceeds the childless maximum, which is all the record shows.

amendments.old: Those earnings, plus $584,850 in bank and stock assets, are far above the aged/blind/disabled income limit and its roughly $2,000 resource cap.
amendments.new: Those earnings, $3,750 a month, exceed SSI's substantial gainful activity limit of $1,690 a month, so PolicyEngine does not count the head as disabled, and $584,850 in bank and stock assets is far above the $2,000 resource cap.
amendments.reason: The engine's income test does not fail here; the disability condition and the asset test do, as the second amendment of this case's note records. Computed for this household on policyengine-us 2.41.0: ssi_earned_income $45,000, so $3,750 a month against gov.ssa.sga.non_blind of $1,690 a month in 2026; ssi_engaged_in_sga True; is_ssi_disabled False; medicaid_optional_senior_or_disabled_countable_income 0 against a limit of $15,960, so the income test passes; ssi_countable_resources 584,850, so the asset test fails; medicaid_category NONE. Indiana's asset limit is $2,000 (assets/limit/individual.yaml), not roughly $2,000.

amendments.old: phases out completely at roughly $26,000 of earned income/AGI for joint filers in 2026
amendments.new: phases out completely at about $26,820 of earned income/AGI for joint filers in 2026
amendments.reason: policyengine-us 2.41.0's 2026 childless EITC for joint filers has a $664 maximum (gov.irs.credits.eitc.max) and phases out at 7.65% (phase_out.rate) from $18,140 (phase_out.start $10,860 plus phase_out.joint_bonus $7,280), so it reaches $0 at $26,820. Computed for a married couple with no children: $62.71 at $26,000 of earnings, $0.06 at $26,819 and $0 at $26,820.
